subject: ventures/social-security-survivor-spousal-benefit-calculator
professional: a Social Security claiming specialist / retirement planner who works from SSA POMS and 20 CFR 404 on survivor and spousal benefits. What they check first: the widow(er)'s limit (RIB-LIM) when the worker claimed early, the survivor age reduction (71.5% at 60), a worker who died before claiming, the spousal excess and how it is reduced when claimed early (25/36 then 5/12 of 1% a month), deemed filing, and that dual entitlement pays the larger benefit, not the sum

evidence.correctness: I ran node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/096f4309-df66-5732-9d71-6aa6a7962eea/scratchpad/ssa/audit.mjs /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/social-security-survivor-spousal-benefit-calculator, which imports the shipped calc.mjs (byte-identical to the served https://marisstella.app/social-security-survivor-spousal-benefit-calculator/calc.mjs, checked with diff). Right: own-benefit factors (72.5% at 62 for a 1957 birth year, 20 CFR 404.410: 5/9 of 1% for 36 months then 5/12), survivor age factor (79.6429% at 62 with survivor FRA 67, linear from 71.5%), delayed credits passed to the survivor (deceased b.1955 claimed at 70: base $4,181.33 = 3200 x 1.30667), and the sample's best total ($988,800 = 120 x $2,288 + 240 x $2,976, hand sum). Wrong, in the cases the tool exists for: (1) RIB-LIM is applied as a base and then reduced again for the survivor's age. Deceased PIA $3,000 claimed at 62 (FRA 67): survivor at 60 should get min(3000 x 0.715, max(2100, 2475)) = $2,145; the tool says $1,769.63 (17.5% low). Deceased claimed at 66: survivor at 63 should be $2,511.43, tool $2,344; at 60 $2,145, tool $2,002. Only the at-FRA figure is right. (2) A worker who died at 63 without claiming is treated as having claimed at 63 (as the input label instructs) so the survivor at FRA is shown $2,475 (82.5%) instead of $3,000 (100%; RIB-LIM applies only when the worker was entitled to a reduced RIB). (3) The spousal top-up applies the spousal reduction to 50% of the worker's PIA and subtracts the unreduced own PIA, instead of reducing the excess (50% worker PIA minus own PIA). Worker PIA $3,000, own PIA $1,000, FRA 67: at 62 the excess should be $500 x 0.65 = $325 (total $1,025), the tool says $0 (total $700); at 64 $375 (total $1,175), tool $125 ($925). The formula is right only when own PIA is 0 or the claim is at FRA. Score 1: the arithmetic runs but the two headline rules a user would act on are wrong for typical inputs.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked by running compute(): survivor benefit table 60-70 (works, numbers wrong before FRA when the worker claimed early), own benefit by age (works), every survivor-first/own-first combination compared (works: 21 x 17 grid in 6-month steps, max(s,o) per month), spousal top-up (present, wrong formula when early), 82.5% limit (present, misapplied), delayed credits inherited (works), text summary download and print (code present, page.test.mjs checks event names), opt-out usage counting (usage.mjs, wired). Gaps: a worker who died before 62 cannot be entered at all (deceasedClaimAge min 62, C5), which is the common case for younger widows claiming at 60; disabled-widow benefits at 50 not mentioned; the widow form and the living-spouse spousal check are mixed into one form keyed off the same 'own PIA' and birth year. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: cd /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/social-security-survivor-spousal-benefit-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 22 tests, 22 pass, 0.16 s; the README's repo-root command also passes 22/22. I seeded 4 mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py; 1 caught (82.5% constant -> 80%), 3 survived: paying the sum of survivor and own benefits instead of the larger one (calc.mjs:78), subtracting the reduced own benefit in the spousal excess (calc.mjs:131), and the 1938-1942 FRA step (calc.mjs:13). Worse, calc.test.mjs:34 asserts the misapplied RIB-LIM as the expected base, and the spousal test (calc.test.mjs:49) only checks a claim at FRA, where the wrong formula and the right one agree. Tests check what the author believed, not SSA rules.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (156 lines), index.html (166), usage.mjs, all three test files. Small, dependency-free, pure functions; parse() rejects rather than clamps and names the field; output is escaped before innerHTML. Defects: HTML inputs say min=0 while parse() enforces 62-70 etc. (only the first error is shown); compute() rounds decimal ages to months silently; the table literal `m <= 840 ? ... : null` is always true (dead branch). Acceptable code for its size; the problems are in the rules, not the code.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present on the page (index.html:111 'No warranty ... not a statement from the Social Security Administration'), README and llms.txt; usage counting with opt-out (index.html:115, usage.mjs). The served page loads (HTTP 200) and the served llms.txt carries marisstella.app URLs, so the source github.io URL is source-only. Failing claims: the FAQ (index.html:12 JSON-LD and :101) says the survivor 'gets the larger of the reduced benefit and 82.5%' when the worker claimed early, which misstates RIB-LIM as a floor; 'Covers: ... the 82.5% widow limit' (index.html:92) is implemented wrong; README:7 'After using this, you know whether to take the survivor benefit now and switch to your own at 70' rests on survivor-before-FRA figures that are low whenever the worker claimed early; the input label (index.html:63) tells a widow whose spouse died before claiming to enter the death age, which produces a wrong 82.5% cap. The spousal FAQ figure (32.5% at 62) is true only with no own record.
evidence.fitness: The job: a recent widow, 60-67, whose spouse claimed at 62 (the most common claiming age), deciding whether to take the survivor benefit now and switch to her own at 70. Walking it with deceased PIA $3,000 claimed at 62 and own PIA $2,000 (b.1962): the tool shows the survivor benefit at 60 as $1,770 instead of $2,145, which understates every survivor-first strategy by about $375 a month during the survivor-only years, the exact comparison the tool sells. A widow whose spouse died at 55 cannot enter the case at all; one whose spouse died at 64 without claiming is told her FRA survivor benefit is 82.5% of PIA rather than 100%. A planner would not hand this to a client.
evidence.domain: Against POMS RS 00615.320 / SSA Act s202(e)(2)(D) (RIB-LIM is a limit on the age-reduced widow(er)'s benefit, applying only when the worker was entitled to a reduced RIB), 20 CFR 404.410 (reduction rates), and POMS/SSA spousal dual-entitlement practice (the excess = 50% of worker PIA minus own PIA, then reduced by 25/36 of 1% for 36 months and 5/12 beyond). Right: survivor age reduction curve, own reduction and DRCs (8%/yr, capped at 70), no DRCs on spousal, survivor not subject to deemed filing (the strategy grid lets survivor and own start independently), dual entitlement pays the larger. Departures: RIB-LIM double reduction, the never-claimed death case, the spousal excess formula, no death-before-62 case. The survivor FRA is a free input (60-67) rather than SSA's table, which the VENTURE.yaml defends but accepts values like 60 that are never a survivor FRA. The POMS section title, fetched with curl from secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0300615320 (HTTP 200; body is script-rendered so only the title was read), is 'RS 00615.320 - Reduced WIB - Deceased NH Entitled to Reduced RIB or Reduced DIB Prior to Death - RIB LIM', which confirms the limit applies only when the worker was entitled to a reduced benefit before death; the cap-not-floor reading is from the Act s202(e)(2)(D) as I know it, not from the fetched body.

defects.what: RIB-LIM is applied as the survivor base and then reduced again for the survivor's age (base = max(reduced RIB, 82.5% PIA), times survivorFactor). The rule is a cap on the age-reduced widow(er) benefit. Deceased PIA $3,000 claimed at 62: survivor at 60 shown $1,769.63, correct $2,145 (17.5% low); every survivor-first strategy total is understated when the worker claimed early.

Spousal excess reduces 50% of the worker's PIA and subtracts the unreduced own PIA, instead of reducing (50% worker PIA - own PIA). Worker $3,000 / own $1,000 at 62: top-up shown $0 (total $700), correct $325 (total $1,025); at 64 $125 vs $375.
A worker who died before claiming is entered as 'claimed at death age' per the input label, so the 82.5% RIB-LIM is applied: death at 63 gives $2,475 at survivor FRA instead of $3,000 (100% PIA).
A worker who died before 62 cannot be entered (deceasedClaimAge min 62), the common case for younger widow(er)s; no way to say 'never claimed'.
FAQ and JSON-LD state RIB-LIM as a floor ('gets the larger of the reduced benefit and 82.5%'), which misinforms readers and search snippets.

Tests encode the wrong rules: calc.test.mjs:34 asserts the misapplied RIB-LIM base, the spousal test only checks a claim at FRA where the wrong formula agrees, and summing survivor and own benefits instead of taking the larger survives (3 of 4 seeded mutations survived).
HTML inputs declare min=0 while parse() enforces 62-70, 60-67 etc.; the survivor FRA input accepts 60, which is never a survivor FRA.

verdict: Small, clean and honest about what it leaves out, with the disclaimer and opt-out usage counting in place, and the own-benefit, survivor age-reduction, DRC and dual-entitlement-max arithmetic is right. But the two rules a claiming specialist checks first are wrong for ordinary inputs: the widow(er)'s limit is reduced twice (survivor at 60 after a worker claimed at 62 shows $1,770 against $2,145), a worker who died before claiming is capped at 82.5% instead of 100%, and the spousal top-up when claimed early is understated or zeroed ($0 vs $325 at 62). The tests (22, all green) assert the wrong RIB-LIM rule and 3 of 4 seeded bugs survived. The FAQ states RIB-LIM backwards. Scores: correctness 1, claims 1, verification 1. Does not meet the bar and is not finished.
